question: Why the original's join_air ends short of its target.

addresses.name: CJoinAirOrder::IsActive
addresses.comment: Slot 14, 0x197BB0 to the last bare `ret` at 0x197D1F (slot 7 starts at 0x197D20). False when the unit has no base. The target (CRef at +0x80) must resolve, must not itself be under a join_air order (0x717), and must hold brigades; then if it stands in the unit's province, CUnit_MergeInto(target, unit), the unit queued for removal, false; else true while CAirOrder::IsActive holds. Any failed test: COrder::OrderReturnToBase and false. The unit given the order is the one that disappears. **Corrected 2026-11-13** (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 67): not every failed test returns home. No base answers false at once (je 0x197D0C) and CAirOrder::IsActive answering false answers false (0x197CE9 -> 0x197D0C), neither calling COrder::OrderReturnToBase; only the target tests (unresolved, itself joining, no brigades) go to 0x197D06 and OrderReturnToBase. The merge asks only that the two share a province (+0x130), not that the target stand still. Confirmed on the running game: Japan's 4. Nihon Koukuujieitai's join is ended by the base test's range return two provinces short of its target.
addresses.evidence: The function disassembled on the running game; MoveUnit and IssueUnitOrder logged for one air group over 27 hours; the hourly saves of two new games read.

addresses.name: CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits
addresses.comment:
**The theatre agent's air groups, every hour it holds one.** Body 0x4CD890-0x4D051D (trap 3: the `ret 8` at 0x4CEE68 is a shared epilogue mid-function). Gate: air_units_count (+0x104) >= 1. Four phases (FINDINGS-reorganise.md, FINDINGS-airnaval4.md): (1) 0x4CDA90 triage of +0xFC (kept by InsertUnitByRange, shortest range first, equals in slot 78's walk order): a dead join_air cancelled; at war, a group whose base province has enemy land units marching in is pulled out of any order but rebase_air and **sets force**; fitness bars 0.5/0.75 at air stance 2, else 0.7/0.85, halved for a CAG or interceptor group; an unfit busy group gets carrier_protection (all CAG, on a carrier) or none; a tired idle group at its base rests. (2) 0x4CE1E9 rebase, only with force: the list is +0x20C (strategic bomber or strategic_attack > 50000), +0x21C (naval bomber), +0x22C (transport plane, and the group is skipped while +0x16C is non-empty) or +0x1FC; the running best starts at the current base province with score 1e6, so the lowest listed base below 1e6 wins and the current one is not scored; a province with enemy land units marching in is skipped; score = the list's float, made (score + DistanceBetweenProvinces(the agent's HQ province, it)) x 0.5 when the group's parent is not at oob level 0; without a transport plane, x load where load = (this pass's arrivals + wings based there + the group's own unless based there) / the air base's level_current, when above 1.0; strict lower wins, first of equals in list (ascending) order; a winner other than the current base gets rebase_air and the arrivals tally moves. (3) 0x4CE64F split and merge. The hinge 0x4CEDA8: a regroup this pass (+0x88) with runs_units or allow_hq_reorg returns 1 with no missions; otherwise missions need force or war and air stance != 0. (4) 0x4CEE76 missions; **the anti-shipping budget is 4 x threatened_provinces_count (+0x1E4)** - the provinces of ours an enemy force at sea is heading for - so a tactical or CAS wing with sea attack flies naval missions only while such a threat stands. The returned bool is not read. The second argument is an int whose byte 3 is read uninitialised and ignored.

**The rebase's crowding, read again 2026-11-10** (`FINDINGS-liveread.md`, section 26): the wings based at a candidate are the regiments of every air unit on the list of the province's air base object (`CMapProvince +0x54`, its list at +4), nested under a headquarters or not, and the group's own are added unless that air base object is the group's (`CUnit +0x98`). On the save of July 1941 Brazil's three bases all score 10000 on every list, and the crowding alone keeps its groups where they are. The CAG test at 0x8CE240 skips a group with any carrier wing before anything else; a group whose own base is not on the list keeps that base when nothing scores under 1e6.

**The triage's four thresholds are two pairs, each used for strength and organisation alike** (`FINDINGS-liveread.md`, section 27): at plan air stance 2 a wing under 0.5 of either is unfit (`[ebp-28]`, `[ebp-3C]` from the float at 0x14BB304 in the running image) and one under 0.75 of either damaged or tired (`[ebp-80]`, `[ebp-A4]`); otherwise 0.7 and 0.85; all halved for a carrier's or an interceptor group. An unfit group under a busy order is called off; a group with any wing damaged or tired, idle at its own base, rests - that is the higher pair, not the unfit one. **'Dead' is COrder's target** (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 51, live 2026-11-11): the triage resolves a join_air's +0x10/+0x14 pair (0x4CDAD8), which a load never sets, so every loaded join_air is called off on entering - Italy's 2nd Squadra Aerea joining the Eolo in August 1938 read id 0. **Read live 2026-11-12** (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 56): the triage lists a group straight away (0x4CE0EC) where the country has neither at_war (+0xACC) nor in_undeclared_war (+0xACD) set, or the group has no base - the fitness, rest and order tests are a country at war's; the split and merge walk the triage's candidate list ([ebp-0xD0], EDI at 0x4CE148) with only the battle, at-own-base, blocking-order and handled tests, and the merge also sets regroup_air_pending at 0x4CEC0F. **Measured 2026-11-13** (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 66): the rebase's crowding counts the air units on the air base's own list, so a carrier's air group based on a carrier in the port is not counted - Britain's first new-game pass sends four single-wing groups to Scapa Flow (level 4) with the Home Fleet's carriers there.

addresses.name: CAIUnit_ManageNavalUnits
addresses.comment:
**The theatre agent's fleets, every pass the tick allows.** Extent 0x4D0880-0x4D3EA1 (the throw tail past the real `ret 8` at 0x4D3E67). Gates: `!force && !at_war (+0xACC) && !in_undeclared_war (+0xACD)` returns; force clears +0x85; no fleet on +0xDC returns; the area is GetArea or the theatre of the unit's province, which must be ours. Phases in order: (1) 0x4D099D withdraw from a losing sea battle (slot-17 ratio against 0.5). (2) 0x4D0B30 **idle fleets home**: a fleet not moving, with no busy order (slot 24) and not at its own base is MoveUnit-ed to its base when CanUnitReach; but a fleet whose definition carries troops (transport_capability >= 1000) stays in port while the plan has an embark (CUnit +0x284); a fleet with no base or an unreachable one is kept on a 'homeless' vector. (3) 0x4D0D70 port and repair, and the 'ready' vector (FINDINGS-agents.md C.3). (4) 0x4D14F0 **existing orders**, per ready fleet: an idle fleet with no destination (+0x2CC) sitting in a port that is not its base is moved to its base, unless it holds a transport and lies in the plan's embark port; a busy fleet: join_fleet - the mover and its target go on the 'handled' list and the port tallies move; a busy transport fleet carrying nothing (CNavy +0x2EC) is cancelled unless CUnit +0x2CA is set; convoy_raid and convoy_escort are cancelled at peace, an escort also when its target is gone; patrol is kept only at war; any other order is kept while the fleet has a destination, cancelled at its own base, and an intercept with no destination away from base is cancelled; cancel = IssueUnitOrder(none) and MoveUnit to the base (or where it is). (5) 0x4D19F6 split and merge (C.3). (6) 0x4D2025 the handled fleets swap-removed from the ready vector (Vector_SwapRemoveValue, which reorders it); +0x27C and +0x280 zeroed; **enemy survey**: every naval unit of every country at war or in undeclared war with us within NavalDistanceTo 1000 of one of the theatre's ports and hostile where it stands (CCountry::IsEnemy) adds GetPower/1000 to +0x27C and goes on a local list, troop carriers (+0x2EC > 0) at the front, the rest at the back. (7) 0x4D2418 per ready fleet: submarine convoy raid, or relocation to the port with most raidable tonnage when fewer than half the route provinces seen are raid candidates, or a surface rebase; the tail adds a free fleet's GetPower/1000 to +0x280 and keeps it free (FINDINGS-airnaval4.md, and FINDINGS-moving.md D). (8) 0x4D323D **patrol**, with naval stance != 0 and (at war, undeclared war or +0x28C > 0): the region V = the +0x284 provinces, or failing any, the sea zone (+0xA4) of each theatre port, both less what CAIUnit_IsBalticBarredToAllies refuses; while V is not empty: centre = V[rand() % |V|] (the C runtime's rand, per thread), the patrol area the centre plus the nearest remaining V entries to it (up to five provinces, each swap-removed from V); the fleet = the nearest free fleet with no busy order, no submarine and at least one screen; `patrol` from now to now + 168 hours over that area; no fleet ends the phase. (9) 0x4D37EA **intercept**, per enemy fleet of the survey list at sea and not Baltic-barred, and only where enemy power (+0x27C) <= own power (+0x280) x 1.5 (2.0 at naval stance 1) unless it carries troops: need = its GetPower/1000, target = need (x 0.66 for a troop carrier); free fleets are gathered nearest first (NavalDistanceTo, strict, first of equals) while 2 x need > gathered, each reachable (CanUnitReach), of non-zero power, not on patrol unless the enemy carries troops, and with a screen when the enemy is all submarines; if gathered >= target, the first gets `intercept` on the enemy fleet and the rest `join_fleet` onto the first, each window now to now, own power reduced and need reduced by each until it falls below zero. Returns 'split or merged a fleet'; slot 73 ignores it.

**Read again 2026-11-10** (`FINDINGS-liveread.md`, section 25). **After the split and merge, an unforced pass ends** (`cmp byte [ebp+0xC], 0` at 0x8D202B): the survey, the per-fleet raid and rebase, the patrol and the intercept run only when the pass is forced - the full pass or replan_naval - at war as at peace. Phase 4's raid, escort and patrol are kept when the country is at war **or in an undeclared war** (+0xACD), not at war alone: on the save of July 1941 the United States is in one, and its Pacific patrols are kept at peace for 48 hours. **Phase 7's tail, on the listing 2026-11-11** (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 42): only a fleet holding no transport (CountShipsByRole out[1] < 1, 0x4D3146) goes on - its power added to +0x280 unless its order is 0x6DE, 0x6E5 or 0x6E9, and it is put on the free list ([esp+0x154], 0x4D3222) where order slot 24 is clear or its order is 0x42E or 0x6E8; the patrol and the intercept take fleets only from that list, so a fleet carrying a transport is sent on neither. **The patrol's rand measured 2026-11-12** (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 53): drawn at 0x4D33E6 on the C runtime's per-thread stream - fresh worker threads from seed 1 (41, 18467, 6334), the main thread carrying on from every draw since the process began; entering July 1941 Germany, Britain, the Soviet Union and the United States drew on the main thread. **The split and merge read 2026-11-12** (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 57): a fleet walked is passed over retreating, fighting, empty, handled, under a blocking order (0x4D1A9A) or away from its own base (0x4D1AA7); a fleet that split a ship off is pushed onto the handled vector at 0x4D1D29 and still looks for a partner; the merge asks fewer than 6 ships by the fleet's own count (+0x40, 0x4D1D45), the split ships not yet gone. **The rebase's entry and scoring, read on the listing 2026-11-13** (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 64): a fleet with no base, or whose base province's theatre (CMapProvince +0x380/+0x384) differs from the agent's theatre (CTheatre +8/+0xC, CObjectId_Differs at 0x4D2E25), is rebased whatever it holds; past that a submarine ends it; a base in another area than the commander's (CUnit +0x1E0 -> +0x130 -> +0x2B4) rebases too; else only a crowded base. The ports are the theatre's (+0x94) in the commander's area, scored by distance to the commander's province + 10.0, + 2000 a ship over the level, x0.75 for the own base; the departure is taken off the old base's arrivals. **The orders that no longer make sense, read on the listing 2026-11-13** (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 65): over each fleet, one with no blocking order (slot 0x60) is passed over while moving (+0x2CC); a join_fleet (0x6E5) is set aside; then a fleet holding a transport (ship definition +0x30), carrying nothing (+0x2EC) and with +0x2CA clear is cancelled whatever its order (0x4D1822); then raid and escort at peace, an escort whose convoy is gone, a patrol at peace, and for a fleet standing still an order at its base or an intercept. The cancel: IssueUnitOrder(none, 0x18D) at 0x4D19A8 and MoveUnit(fleet, base, 0, 0, 0, 0) at 0x4D19BD.

addresses.name: CJoinFleetOrder::IsActive
addresses.comment: Slot 14 (COrder's IsActive), 0x19BC40-0x19BD78, bare `ret`s. **Where a join_fleet order does its merge.** False when the fleet has no base. Otherwise, while CNavalOrder::IsActive holds: the target fleet (0x19BBF0); where it exists and is not the fleet itself, then if the two stand in **the same province** CUnit_MergeInto(target, fleet) - every ship and every carried land unit go to the **target**, which keeps its name and id - the fleet is queued for removal and the order ends (false); if not yet together, true (still sailing). No target, or itself: COrder::OrderReturnToBase and false. So the unit given the order is the one that disappears. **Measured 2026-11-13** (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 65): the merge does not wait for the target to stand still - a light cruiser joining France's transport fleet merged into it at sea while it crawled for want of fuel.
